title: Dogfood: deploy Private VPC Terraform modules in internal sandbox and capture punch list
creator: Irene Choi
description:
Goal
- Validate that the alpha VPC Terraform modules can be applied end-to-end in a clean AWS account with Redwood-default assumptions for Private deployments.
- Capture issues, gaps, and risky defaults before design partner pilots.
- Produce a punch list with owners + links to PRs/tickets.

Scope of dogfood
- Stand up core networking footprint via `redwood-terraform` modules:
  - VPC + public/private subnets + routing/NAT defaults
  - VPC endpoints + Private DNS behaviors
  - VPC Flow Logs default destinations
  - Opinionated security group patterns (cluster nodes + egress)
  - IAM scaffold for installer execution role + permission boundary support
- Validate basic installer preflight compatibility (no full EKS/app install in this ticket; focus on network prerequisites and outputs).

Environment
- Account: Redwood sandbox AWS account provisioned via INT-1734 (restricted budget + guardrails)
- Region: us-west-2
- AZs tested: 2 AZ and 3 AZ layouts (to exercise NAT/subnet mapping)
- CIDR used: 10.80.0.0/16
- Terraform: pinned per repo defaults (see PR-18503)

How we tested
1) `terraform fmt/validate` locally
2) `terraform apply` from a fresh state (no pre-existing VPC resources)
3) Verified expected outputs are present and usable by installer:
   - vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids
   - endpoint IDs and DNS enablement flags
   - security group IDs for nodes/egress
   - IAM role ARN for installer execution
4) Smoke checks:
   - Confirm private subnets have egress via NAT by default (where enabled)
   - Confirm endpoint Private DNS works for ECR/ST S/CloudWatch Logs (where enabled)
   - Confirm Flow Logs deliver to the chosen destination
5) `terraform destroy` and re-apply to check idempotency + cleanup

Outcomes
- Overall: modules are close to pilot-ready for “standard” VPC footprint. Primary rough edges are around AZ assumptions, endpoint coverage, and clearer guardrails/docs for Private DNS + strict egress.
- Apply time: ~14–22 minutes depending on endpoint set + number of AZs (NAT GW creation dominates)
- Destroy time: ~8–12 minutes
- Cost notes: NAT GW + endpoints are the main drivers. Leaving a dogfood stack up overnight cost ~$10–$20 depending on endpoint count. We should call this out in the integration test harness (nightly vs per-PR).

Key issues found (with resolution / linkage)
1) NAT gateway AZ mapping assumptions (BLOCKER for 3-AZ)
- Symptom: private subnet route table associations were incorrect when `az_count=3`; one AZ had no functional egress.
- Root cause: module assumed a 1:1 ordering between public subnets and NAT GWs that wasn’t stable across `for_each` ordering.
- Fix: PR-18605 “fix NAT gateway availability zone assumptions” (merged).
- Follow-up: add explicit validation that `nat_gateway_mode=one_per_az` requires public subnet count == AZ count.

2) Missing or misconfigured ECR endpoints -> installer image pull failures
- Symptom: when Private DNS was disabled (or ECR endpoints not included), nodes could not resolve/pull ECR images; installer fails with “unable to pull image” style errors.
- Cross-reference: SUP-28411 and installer PR-19110 (preflight checks for required endpoints + warning on missing ECR).
- Action: ensure module example includes ECR API + ECR DKR endpoints by default for private clusters; ensure docs are explicit about Private DNS requirements and alternatives (proxy/egress).

3) Endpoint Private DNS behavior not obvious; surprises for corp DNS setups
- Symptom: enabling Private DNS for some endpoints conflicted with customer-managed DNS forwarding patterns (observed internally when testing split-horizon resolvers).
- Decision: keep Private DNS enabled by default for the “standard” footprint, but document supported override patterns and explicitly warn about hybrid DNS complexity.
- Cross-reference: architecture discussion in Slack architecture thread (1749014421).

4) Flow Logs destination + retention defaults need to be clearer
- Symptom: Flow Logs to CloudWatch defaulted to log group creation, but retention was not consistently set in one path; also unclear when to prefer customer-owned S3 bucket.
- Cross-reference: PR-18455 (flow logs and destination options) + Security guidance doc.
- Action: set a consistent retention default (e.g., 30 days) for CloudWatch in alpha; require explicit S3 bucket ARN if `destination=s3` (do not auto-create by default for least surprise).

5) Security group egress defaults too permissive for regulated expectations
- Symptom: default egress rule allowed 0.0.0.0/0 on node SG when NAT was enabled (operable but not “secure by default” for a Private story).
- Resolution direction: provide a “strict egress” mode that routes egress primarily to VPC endpoints + explicitly allowed CIDRs (customer proxy, SIEM, etc.), while keeping an “operable” mode for alpha.
- Cross-reference: PR-18474 (SG patterns) debate; Security thread (1749130099).

6) Output naming mismatches / missing outputs for installer integration
- Symptom: installer docs expect a stable set of output names; we found a couple outputs missing (endpoint security group id, selected endpoint list).
- Action: add/standardize outputs in the endpoints and IAM modules; align with installer integration docs (PR-19144).

Punch list (actionable follow-ups)
- [Victor Alvarez] Add validation and clearer errors for NAT/AZ constraints (tie to ENG-4829 interface hardening)
- [Bruno Silva] Expand “standard endpoints” set and make ECR endpoints non-optional in examples (tie to ENG-4844)
- [Kevin Osei / Allison Grant] Confirm Flow Logs retention defaults and SIEM hooks language; update module README + Confluence doc (tie to ENG-4852)
- [Hanae Suzuki / Marcus Lin] Propose “strict egress” security group mode + document trade-offs (tie to PR-18474 follow-up)
- [Sahana Iyer] Adjust integration test strategy to run heavy apply/destroy nightly; per-PR runs only fmt/validate/tflint/checkov (tie to ENG-4860)
- [Nina Petrova] Confirm EKS private control plane constraints and required endpoints list is complete for installer preflight checks (tie to ENG-4869)

Links
- Confluence reference architecture: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/aws-private-vpc-reference-architecture-eks.json
- Deployment guide: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/terraform-vpc-deployment-guide-alpha.json
- Release/versioning standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards/terraform-module-versioning-and-release-process.json
- Relevant PRs:
  - PR-18422 (core VPC module)
  - PR-18437 (endpoints + Private DNS)
  - PR-18455 (flow logs)
  - PR-18474 (SG patterns)
  - PR-18491 (IAM scaffold)
  - PR-18503 (lint/security scan + provider pinning)
  - PR-18519 (integration test harness)
  - PR-18605 (NAT AZ bugfix)
- Installer alignment:
  - PR-19110 (preflight check for missing ECR endpoints)
  - PR-19144 (installer docs for Terraform integration)

Risks / notes
- Alpha customers with strict egress will need more guidance (proxy patterns, allowlists, endpoint completeness). We should treat “no 0.0.0.0/0 egress” as a first-class documented mode, even if it’s not the default in the first alpha drop.
- CI cost: if we run full apply/destroy on every PR, costs + time will be non-trivial. Recommend nightly plus manual trigger for release candidates.

Definition of done
- Dogfood apply/destroy completed in sandbox for 2-AZ and 3-AZ.
- All issues logged with links to PRs or follow-up tickets.
- Key blocker (NAT AZ assumption) resolved prior to pilot kickoff.
- Summary posted to #eng-infra and #eng-private-deployments with punch list and owners.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Successful terraform apply and destroy in a clean sandbox account for 2-AZ and 3-AZ footprints. 2) Validate module outputs meet Redwood Private installer expectations (VPC/subnets/endpoints/SG/IAM). 3) Publish punch list with owners and links to follow-up work. 4) Identify any pilot-blocking issues and either fix or explicitly document as alpha limitation.

final_summary: Dogfood completed in sandbox (2-AZ + 3-AZ). Identified and fixed a pilot-blocking NAT AZ mapping bug (PR-18605). Logged remaining gaps around endpoint completeness (ECR), Private DNS clarity for hybrid DNS, Flow Logs retention defaults, and SG strict egress mode. Recommended CI strategy: nightly integration applies, per-PR static checks only.
